stories.title: An informatics workflow for label-scarce cross-domain segmentation of geological outcrop fractures from UAV photogrammetric imagery
stories.description: Accurate extraction of geological outcrop fracture networks from UAV photogrammetric imagery supports rock-mass characterization, discontinuity mapping, and geotechnical interpretation. However, automated segmentation remains challenging because fractures are often thin, low-contrast, discontinuous, and visually confused with heterogeneous textures, weathering patterns, and shadows. Pixel-level annotation is also labor-intensive, resulting in limited labeled data for newly surveyed areas. This study develops a label-scarce cross-domain segmentation workflow using GeoCrack as the source domain and RockCrack, a small, site-specific UAV dataset, as the target domain. GRNet, the segmentation model used in the workflow, combines Deformable Large-Kernel Attention at the bottleneck with Spatial-Channel Squeeze-and-Excitation in the encoder. Feature-space analysis identifies a measurable discrepancy between the two domains. On GeoCrack, GRNet achieves an IoU of 66.84% and an F1-score of 80.12%. When trained from scratch on RockCrack, it achieves a five-fold mean crack-class IoU of 56.69 ± 4.34% and an F1-score of 72.28 ± 3.61%. Following GeoCrack pretraining and target-domain fine-tuning, the best-performing configuration achieves a mean IoU of 58.96 ± 3.64% and an F1-score of 74.13 ± 2.93%. Fine-tuning substantially outperforms direct source-only deployment, although differences between the leading strategies are small and fold-dependent. The workflow provides pixel-level fracture maps that can support subsequent skeletonization, trace vectorization, and fracture-network characterization; however, further spatial calibration, uncertainty assessment, and geological validation are required before the outputs can be used for quantitative rock-mass analysis or engineering decisions.

stories.title: YOLO-FWF: a lightweight frequency-wavelet feature fusion network for robust scene text detection
stories.description: Scene text detection remains challenging due to large scale variations, slender stroke structures, complex backgrounds, low contrast, and arbitrary text orientations. To address these issues, this paper proposes YOLO-FWF, an improved lightweight scene text detection model based on YOLO11n. First, a C3k2_FrequencyCM module is introduced into the backbone to enhance fine-grained text representation by combining Fourier-domain amplitude compensation with spatial high-frequency feature enhancement, thereby improving the sensitivity of the network to text strokes, edges, and weak texture cues. Second, a C2PSA_WDAM module is designed to replace the original C2PSA structure. By decomposing features into low-frequency semantic components and high-frequency detail components through wavelet transform, the module uses high-frequency information to guide attention modeling and suppress background interference. Third, a Fourier Angle Alignment Fusion module is proposed for multi-scale feature fusion. It estimates dominant local orientations in the frequency domain and aligns high-level semantic features with low-level structural features before fusion, improving the detection of inclined, curved, and irregular text instances. Experiments on two Roboflow-hosted scene text datasets demonstrate that YOLO-FWF achieves superior detection accuracy while maintaining a lightweight structure. On the text scene computer vision dataset, YOLO-FWF reaches 86.8% mAP50 and 64.2% mAP50:95 with only 2.89 M parameters and 6.7 GFLOPs. On the text detection dataset, it achieves 54.7% mAP50 and 34.6% mAP50:95, outperforming YOLO11n and other mainstream detectors under the same evaluation setting. These results verify the effectiveness of frequency-domain enhancement, wavelet-guided attention, and direction-aware feature fusion on the evaluated datasets. Because the current experiments do not include standard public scene-text benchmarks, broader generalization remains to be further verified.
